# When bergfex Says No

A pre-release, published for [#57](https://github.com/timmaurice/bergfex/issues/57): every entry on one installation fails with `403, message='Forbidden'` and nothing in the log says why.

**This does not try to fix the 403.** It makes it legible. The cause is not reproducible from anywhere else — the pages return 200 with every user agent and over the same library the integration uses — so the next step is evidence, not a guess.

## What is new

- **A refusal now says what refused.** bergfex sits behind Cloudflare, and a block carries its reason in the response body and a ray id in the headers. Both were thrown away before anything was read, so a report could only ever say `403, message='Forbidden'`. The status, the Cloudflare ray id, the server, and the first 512 characters of the block page are now kept. The page itself is never pulled in to be discarded — a bergfex page is around 200 KB.
- **Both urls, not just the last one.** bergfex redirects German resorts from `www.bergfex.at` to `www.bergfex.de`, so the url in the error was the end of a redirect, not what the integration asked for. That sent one report looking for a host no released version has ever offered. Requested and final url are now reported side by side whenever they differ.
- **A repair notice instead of silent retrying.** After five consecutive refusals — about two and a half minutes, so a restart or a short outage does not trigger it — Home Assistant shows a notice naming the host, the status and the ray id, instead of counting up a backoff forever with no explanation. One notice per host, however many resorts sit behind it. It clears itself the moment a single request gets through.
- **The diagnostics download carries it.** An entry that is being refused never finishes setting up, which means it has no coordinator and so had nothing useful in its diagnostics — and that is precisely the entry a bug report is attached to. The refusal evidence now sits outside that block.
- **A 404 is not a refusal.** A wrong path and a bad day at bergfex are told apart from being turned away; only 403, 429 and 451 raise the notice.

## If you are seeing 403

Install this, let it retry a few times, then attach the **diagnostics download** (⋮ on the entry → Download diagnostics) to the issue. It carries the ray id, which is what bergfex would need to look up which rule answered.

One thing worth saying plainly: if your address is being refused, there may be nothing the integration can do about it. What it can now do is tell you so, and give you something to hand on.

## Not in this release

The user agent is unchanged, on purpose. A release whose job is to observe must not change behaviour at the same time, or a green result proves nothing.
